text:
I’ll verify only the listing-scope correction against the round-1 leak: authoritative drives must stay narrowed, and open drives must stay open.## Verdict: GREEN

The round-1 leak is closed. `grantFilteringApplies()` stays true when any registered profile still has grant narrowing (`NodeReadRepository.php:492-503`). `candidateNodeIds()` then unions two sets (`NodeReadRepository.php:525-579`):

- Grant anchors and their descendants stay limited to drives whose selected driver is grant-authoritative and whose grants feature is on.
- Node ids from only the other drives — a non-authoritative driver, or grants disabled — are added beside that set.

A sibling `gate` or `grants(false)` profile no longer makes the predicate false. `PanelAccessScope` therefore keeps a real id list (`PanelAccessScope.php:43-47`), and `DriveResource`, `NodeGrantResource`, `NodeShareResource`, and `ActivityResource` keep their `whereIn` predicates. An authoritative drive with no grant for the actor stays out of that list, so its drive row, grant, share, and activity rows stay out of those queries.

A pure open installation still returns false from `grantFilteringApplies()`, so `PanelAccessScope` returns null and `constrainToAccessible()` leaves the caller query unchanged (`NodeReadRepository.php:421-422`). The open drive in a mixed installation is still included through `openIds`, including when the authoritative side has anchors and the union is taken. Exact node checks are unchanged.

`validation.json#correction` records exit 0 for the 35-test core listing slice, the 6-test Filament listing file, core and Filament PHPStan, and Pint on the two changed files. This review did not re-run them.
thought:
Verifying source implementation coherence with the correction and checking union logic.

grantFilteringApplies returns false only when no profile is authoritative with grants enabled. candidateNodeIds unions all node IDs for non-authoritative or grants-disabled drives against grant anchors scoped to authoritative drives.

Empty anchors correctly return openIds only. When anchors exist, openIds merge into the id map before adding anchors and descendants. The test confirms open drives are included while hidden authoritative drives are excluded. All-open installations correctly disable grant filtering.

PanelAccessScope returns null when no profile is authoritative, leaving queries unfiltered. constrainToAccessible exits early and preserves the original query when grant filtering is inactive.

An edge case with an authoritative profile that owns no drives still behaves correctly: all actual drives remain open, so candidateNodeIds returns their node IDs without applying grant filtering.

The filtering check is per-drive. A drive with grants disabled under its own profile is fully open, while a sibling drive using the default authoritative profile remains narrowed by grant anchors.

The correction now calls forProfile before checking grants. Previously, drives with disabled grants were skipped entirely. If a drive.profile points to a registry entry that does not exist, forProfile throws; this is preexisting fail-closed behavior and outside the scope of this fix.

A missing registry profile now throws instead of skipping the drive. This is fail-closed and not a leak, though it may be stricter than the old skip behavior.

The missing-profile behavior is preexisting. VaulterConfig::featureEnabled already calls ProfileRegistry::get($profile), so the old code would throw on an unregistered profile during grants checks. This change does not introduce a regression.

Open drive node IDs are added directly to the candidate set without subtree expansion. Descendant traversal only applies to authoritative anchors, so open drive nodes cannot be duplicated through cross-drive descendant walks.

Descendant IDs remain storage-scoped, so cross-drive subtree expansion cannot leak hidden nodes. The test confirms the actor cannot see hidden authoritative nodes. Visible and open drives still appear in the DriveResource query.

DriveResource filters by root_node_id against the candidate set. Visible drives include their root ID because the owner holds a grant on it. Open drives include all node IDs including the root. Hidden drives exclude their root ID because the owner lacks a grant.

NodeGrantResource and NodeShareResource filter by node_id. Hidden grants and shares are excluded because their target node IDs are absent from the candidate set.

ActivityResource filters by target_id.

ActivityResource filters by target_id against the candidate set. The test does not assert that activity rows are excluded when their target is a hidden node, so the assertion passes vacuously if no such row exists. This is a test gap rather than a product leak, since the underlying query predicate remains identical.

Checking whether the test actually creates activity rows for hidden grants, shares, or folders. Also verifying that candidateNodeIds merges open drive IDs without dropping descendants or double-opening authoritative nodes.

A potential regression surfaced: open drives now pluck all node IDs without applying a whereNull trashed_at filter. Previously the caller's own query unchanged preserved its existing trash filtering. This could expose trashed nodes in open drive listings.

The trashed-node concern is harmless. Extra IDs in the candidate set that do not match the caller's query are ignored, so no leak occurs.

Plucking node IDs by drive_id prevents cross-drive contamination.

Storage-scoped subtree traversal keeps descendant nodes within their own drive, preventing leakage into open or hidden drives.

The candidate set ordering is safe: open IDs are merged first, then anchors, then descendants. Descendant expansion only pulls from the actor’s own granted anchors, so hidden nodes cannot leak through subtree traversal.

A grant on a hidden drive correctly includes it in the candidate set.

The fix checks each drive’s own profile rather than the global driver. A drive using the `open` profile resolves to a non-authoritative gate driver, while the default profile resolves to an authoritative database driver.

The `grants(false)` open profile short-circuits to the unfiltered open lane because `featureEnabled` returns false. The global database driver being authoritative is irrelevant here.

If global grants are disabled, every profile fails the check and `grantFilteringApplies` returns false. This forces all listings into the fully open path.

The test registers a default profile without a permission driver, so it falls back to the global database driver and keeps grants enabled. The open drive uses the 'open' profile. Grants, shares, and folders are created before the registry swap, meaning any activity rows generated by those actions would already exist when the queries run.

I need to verify whether DriveBuilder records activity for hidden nodes. If it does not, the test assertion is vacuous and cannot catch a product leak. The underlying query predicate remains unchanged, so a vacuous check does not reopen the vulnerability. I will flag this only if the query itself is incorrect.

When filtering is active but the actor has no anchors and no open drives, candidateNodeIds returns an empty array and constrainToAccessible correctly applies a whereRaw 1=0 deny. An open drive with zero nodes still includes its root_node_id in the candidate set if one exists.

A node cannot appear on both an open drive and an authoritative anchor, so ID collisions are impossible. The diff was truncated at the subtreeAnchorIds line, but the remainder of candidateNodeIds is unchanged. I will verify that anchors and descendants are still added to the candidate set and that array_values returns the final list.

grantFilteringApplies checks the profile registry, while candidateNodeIds checks drives. A drive with an authoritative profile is narrowed, but a registered authoritative profile does not open other drives. A drive whose profile flag disables grants opens entirely; this is intended. A subclass of Database that isGrantAuthoritative false also opens entirely, leaving sibling database drives narrowed.

Spatie, Azgard, and Gate drives do not implement GrantAuthoritativeDriver. They open entirely while sibling database drives remain narrowed. A null driver such as NonProduction also opens fully, so mixed configurations keep database profiles narrowed and other drivers open.

Open drives still expose all nodes to the actor, including those the role driver would normally restrict. This is preexisting behavior for non-authoritative drivers and was explicitly required by the finding. Exact node authorization remains in ListNodes. The correction preserves this per-drive behavior without introducing a new blocker.

The test asserts that the open node is contained and the hidden node is excluded, but it does not assert that the visible root is contained. The visible root should still be in the candidate set because the owner holds a grant on it, though this is not explicitly checked. The constrainToAccessible assertion also omits the hidden root; only the hidden folder node is verified as absent.

A drive with no grants for the owner is correctly excluded from candidates. The test does not depend on item-scope grant behavior for child folders. When anchors are empty, the method returns open IDs early without adding descendants. When anchors exist, descendant IDs are appended after open IDs, and the union preserves the open set.

The test swaps the profile registry after saving drives with the 'open' profile, but before the queries run. Both `featureEnabled` and `forProfile` resolve the same container instance, so the replacement is visible to both checks.

The Gate driver must be registered in the permission_drivers configuration for forProfile('open') to resolve. The six passing filament tests imply this registration exists, so I will not re-run them.Checking a potential hole: activity rows for hiddenNode.

DriveBuilder::folder writes activity for hiddenNode. The query excludes hiddenNode from candidates, so the row is filtered out. The test assertion not->toContain hiddenNode is valid if the row's target is hiddenNode; otherwise it passes even when the row is visible.

Confirmed: the test proves hiddenNode activity rows are filtered. Now checking if activity rows targeting the hidden drive's root are a remaining bug.

Activity rows targeting the hidden drive's root are also excluded when the root is absent from candidates. This is not a leak.

Pure open behavior is preserved: without an authoritative profile, grant filtering returns false and resources remain unfiltered.

A remaining question is whether a pure gate installation still has a default database profile; if the default profile's permission driver is null, forProfile falls back to the global gate.

If the default profile is database and global permission driver is gate, drives on that default remain authoritative and filtering stays active. This is correct behavior.

A potential remaining hole: if a drive uses a profile string that is neither the open profile nor the default, grantFilteringApplies might still evaluate to true incorrectly.

Another potential issue: authoritative drives are narrowed using subjects.

Open drives include all node IDs in the candidate set, even those the gate would deny. This preserves the open lane. Grants on an open drive remain visible to everyone because all its node IDs are included. The test does not assert this visibility, but it is intentional behavior. It is not a leak of the hidden authoritative drive.

DescendantIdsOf cannot pull nodes from the hidden drive. Subtree anchors are filtered to the authoritative drive's reachable nodes, and a grant on the visible root's descendants stays confined to that drive. The early return when anchors is empty also correctly returns openIds without deduplication.

The activity resource also filters by target_type, so hidden node targets are excluded. DriveBuilder::storage() does not auto-grant the creating actor, since the tests confirm hidden drives remain hidden.

The explicit grant is only on the visible root. The user confirmed the tests passed, so validation.json#correction should be checked to confirm execution. The PanelAccessScope doc is slightly stale but behaviorally correct for pure open.

NodeResource getEloquentQuery uses constrainToAccessible. The SQL candidate set includes open drive nodes and visible grant nodes, but never hidden authoritative nodes. ListNodes exact-filters the page, so hidden nodes never appear in results. Open drive nodes enter the query and are then filtered by the exact filter to hide gate-denied items. This is correct behavior.

The verdict is GREEN.Verifying the log summary counts of 35 and 6 passed tests to avoid contradicting the user.

The correction appears correct. I am now checking for any remaining edge-case blockers.

The descendant walk from authoritative anchors is already drive-scoped. Open drive nodes are additive and do not introduce cross-drive leaks. No remaining blockers found.

The edge case where all drives are open and the default profile is authoritative was verified. The candidate set becomes the union of all open drive nodes, with no authoritative drives to leak. Any node missing a drive or outside the cursor is correctly excluded.

Soft-deleted drives excluded from the cursor are a preexisting limitation, not a new leak. Pure open installations never apply the candidateNodeIds predicate, so they remain unaffected.
